thread:
sasha: heads up NA-west reporting degraded GPU capacity and a sudden latency spike across runtime v2 nodes, started ~10:12 UTC. p95 token latency jumped from 120ms -> 850ms. seeing high KV cache miss rates and large batch tails.

alex: on it. is this correlating with the autoscaler churn earlier?

sasha: maybe. autoscaler did several evictions 10:05-10:10. but logs show a recent deploy to runtime-v2 at 09:58 that changed batching defaults. suspecting batching/kvcache regression.

maria: confirmed error logs from runtime: "KVCache: invalidation miss ratio 0.78" and a lot of GC churn on the field nodes. attaching snippet:

maria: ```
[10:11:23] KVCache::Miss rate: 0.78
[10:11:27] BatchQueue: avg batch size 36, tail latency 1200ms
[10:11:30] runtime-worker: oom_killer invoked (soft)
```

jun: re: deploys - deploy-bot shows a config patch at 09:58: `runtime-config.batch.max_size: 64 -> 128` and `kvcache.prefix_enabled: true` rolled out to all NA-west replicas.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) rollback batch max_size to 64 for NA-west canary nodes, 2) temporarily disable prefix KV caching, 3) shift 25% traffic to NA-east. agree?

sasha: +1. also recommend disabling preemptible GPU scheduling for new pods in NA-west until we stabilise. current spot churn is making things worse.

maria: running commands now:

maria: ```
# rollback batch size for runtime-v2 deployment to 64 (canary)
kubectl -n runtime patch deploy runtime-v2 --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/0/value","value":"64"}]' --context=cluster-na-west

# disable prefix kvcache via feature flag
kubectl -n runtime patch cm runtime-flags -p '{"data":{"kvcache_prefix":"false"}}' --context=cluster-na-west
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: patch applied to runtime-v2 (canary) at 10:17 UTC.

deploy-bot: rolling update started for runtime-v2-canary (3 pods) -> expected 6m.

jun: routing runbook - shifting traffic: calling routing API to add fallback policy, move 25% route weight to na-east-pool.

alex: also lowering `max_concurrency` for affected routes to reduce batch tail. set to 8 -> will throttle clients if needed but lowers latency.

sasha: cost note: shifting 25% to NA-east increases egress and cross-region RPS costs; estimate ~+$2.5k/day if sustained. we should monitor spend vs user impact.

maria: can we instead spin up hotpool in NA-west with reserved GPUs? that avoids cross-region cost but slower to provision. we have 12 reserved GPUs available but need kube quotas adjusted.

jun: raised quota change request to infra-quotas, but will take ~15m. with rollback and kvcache disable we should see p95 improve sooner.

ops-bot: metrics: p95 latency (NA-west) dropped to 320ms at 10:25 after canary patch, KV miss down to 0.32. still degraded vs normal.

alex: good. continue canary rollout to 50% if p95 < 400ms and error rate < 0.5%. otherwise rollback fully.

maria: starting canary -> full NA-west patch now. patch will run with maxUnavailable=1.

deploy-bot: runtime-v2 patch progressed to 60% at 10:34.

sasha: alert - one node in na-west-az3 shows kernel OOM tracebacks, evicting pods. mark that AZ as degraded, reduce traffic to it.

jun: updated routing: az3 weight -> 0 for 12m. redirect to az1/az2 within NA-west and to NA-east fallback.

ops-bot: p95 now 210ms at 10:42, KV miss 0.12. error rate steady at 0.2%.

alex: rolling back the `batch.max_size` experiment and disabling prefix kvcache fixed most of the regression. follow-ups: 1) revert feature flags in git, 2) add pre-deploy perf gate for batch config changes, 3) investigate why autoscaler evicted healthy pods (eviction storms).

sasha: agree. filing follow-up issues and scheduling postmortem. will keep NA-west in restricted mode (no spot) for next 24h while we validate.

maria: creating incident ticket: INC-2027-847. brief notes + runbook recorded.

jun: thanks all. ops: any lingering tasks?

alex: reopen if p95 > 300ms. otherwise close this thread after postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident INC-2027-847 created, severity P2, assigned to eng-infra.

sasha: closing loop here — partial mitigation succeeded, follow-up actions assigned.
